speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (a) whether he can provide an update on the Singapore Islamic College and its tie-in with the Postgraduate Certificate in Islam in Contemporary Societies (PCICS) programme, including its take-up rate and efficacy; and (b) whether any changes will be made to the PCICS programme in terms of (i) duration (ii) content and (iii) accessibility.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It enables MUIS to build up experience and a body of knowledge to develop a curriculum for tertiary studies in collaboration with international partners.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In addition, MUIS launched the Research Programme on Communities of Success (RPCS) in June 2021 to grow its capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The research programme aims to develop knowledge on emerging socio-religious issues experienced by minority Muslim communities living in secular states and advanced economies.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The PCICS and RPCS will enable MUIS to build a strong foundation to develop respected religious leaders that will guide our Muslim community to thrive in Singapore, contributing to our community of success.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: My first supplementary question is with regard to the graduates themselves and the current programme, whether we can include internship programmes within this course where they are given opportunities to go into the community to do some social service or work where they can acclimatise themselves further into our society.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: My second supplementary question is with regard to a series of discussions I conducted with current students overseas, mainly in Jordan and Egypt.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Generally, they are receptive and supportive of the course but they also shared some concerns.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: One of them is that the course, being a year long, they are wondering whether part of it, since there is an online element, could be done when they are studying overseas.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In this way, when they come back, it cuts down the course duration and they can get into the workforce sooner.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The PCICS is a programme that was co-created by the community of asatizah and was led by Dr Mohamad Maliki Osman, then Senior Minister of State, when he chaired the Committee on Future Asatizah (COFA).

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But I think the most important thing to preserve is the rigour of the curriculum.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I agree with the Member that we do have to have some elements of internship but we do have to balance that with the justifiable comment that the length of the course must also be not just adequate but also appropriate.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will update Members later when there are new developments as we run a few more terms of the PCICS and after more cohorts have graduated from the course.
